hn.originalTitle: AI agents fake identities, target real people in new security incident
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Anthropic AI agent fakes identities, targets real people in new security incident | CNN Business

The logo of the AI assistant "Claude Mythos" built by the US firm Anthropic displayed on a smartphone's screen in Brussels on June 10, 2026. Nicolas Tucat/AFP/Getty Images AI UK See all topics Facebook Tweet Email Link Threads Link Copied! Follow Anthropic’s most advanced artificial intelligence model used fake identities to deceive real people and try to plant malicious code during testing by Britain’s AI Security Institute (AISI) –– the latest example of an AI model going rogue.

Anthropic and OpenAI models were tested with lowered security guardrails in lab environments, but, in a first, were found to engage in “social engineering” to pressure a human approver while carrying out an unsanctioned task, the government research lab said.

“This is the first time AISI has seen deception of this severity that was targeted at a real person, unprompted, in the real world,” the institute said Tuesday . There has been no evidence of real-world harm, it added.

The security incident is the latest in a string of examples of advanced AI models engaging in unauthorized actions, events that have prompted growing calls for more government action to regulate artificial intelligence and even to slow its pace of development.

Both OpenAI and Anthropic reported their models escaping testing environments and hacking into other systems in late July. But unlike these earlier reported security breaches, the British institute explicitly gave the models internet access during its testing.

Among the 122 cybersecurity challenges the institute ran, it found that in 10 of those runs, AI agents “took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organizations,” with most of them stemming from Anthropic’s Mythos 5 model and the rest from OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol.

In the most serious incident, the agent attempted to get approval from human reviewers to “insert malicious code into a publicly used open-source project” by creating “multiple fake identities,” according to the institute.

The agent “tried to contact real people directly, sending messages and files through an online file-transfer service to persuade them, or their own AI coding tools, to run malicious code,” it said. After the agent’s actions were challenged, it then modified earlier records and considered using a new identity to continue.

People walk past the Moonshot booth promoting its Kimi K3 AI model, during the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, China, July 17, 2026. Go Nakamura/Reuters What is China’s Kimi K3 and why is the US so rattled by it?

The institute’s disclosure came on the same day representatives from the top AI companies met with the White House to discuss the new framework where the government will review the most advanced AI models before they’re released publicly.

In a statement on X , Anthropic said the models were tested under “deliberately permissive conditions” with the removal of safeguards and no specific restrictions on how the internet should be used.

“We’re working closely with them to gather more details of the incident as we conduct our own investigation,” it said, adding that there was no evidence of an escape from a secure environment.

OpenAI identified the two unsanctioned actions as crossing outside the test environment and engage in actions unrequired for the exercises.

“We are committed to working across the industry to strengthen shared practices for conducting high-risk evaluations safely,” it said in a Tuesday company blog post .

hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
人類人工智慧代理在新的安全事件中偽造身份，以真人為目標 | CNN Business 2026 年 6 月 10 日，美國公司 Anthropic 打造的人工智慧助手「Claude Mythos」的標誌顯示在布魯塞爾的智慧型手機螢幕上。 Nicolas Tucat/AFP/Getty Images AI UK 查看所有主題 Facebook 推文 電子郵件連結 主題連結 已複製！關注 Anthropic 最先進的人工智慧模型，在英國人工智慧安全研究所 (AISI) 的測試過程中，使用虛假身份來欺騙真人，並試圖植入惡意程式碼——這是人工智慧模型失控的最新例子。政府研究實驗室表示，人類和 OpenAI 模型在實驗室環境中的安全護欄較低的情況下進行了測試，但首先被發現參與“社會工程”，在執行未經批准的任務時向人類審批者施加壓力。該研究所週二表示：「這是 AISI 第一次在現實世界中發現針對真人、未經提示的如此嚴重的欺騙行為。」它補充說，沒有證據表明現實世界受到傷害。這次安全事件是一系列高級人工智慧模型參與未經授權的行動的例子中的最新一起，這些事件促使越來越多的人呼籲政府採取更多行動來監管人工智慧，甚至放慢人工智慧的發展速度。

OpenAI 和 Anthropic 都報告稱，他們的模型在 7 月下旬逃離了測試環境並入侵了其他系統。但與先前報告的安全漏洞不同的是，英國研究所在測試期間明確允許模型存取網路。在該研究所開展的 122 項網路安全挑戰中，發現在其中 10 項中，人工智慧代理“在實時互聯網上針對真實的人和組織採取了自主的、未經批准的行動”，其中大多數源於 Anthropic 的 Mythos 5 模型，其餘來自 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6-Sol。該研究所表示，在最嚴重的事件中，該特工試圖透過創建「多個虛假身份」來獲得人類審查人員的批准，以「將惡意程式碼插入公開使用的開源專案中」。該特工「試圖直接聯繫真實的人，透過線上文件傳輸服務發送訊息和文件，說服他們或他們自己的人工智慧編碼工具運行惡意程式碼，」它說。在特工的行為受到質疑後，它修改了先前的記錄並考慮使用新的身份繼續。 2026 年 7 月 17 日，在中國上海舉行的世界人工智慧大會上，人們走過宣傳其 Kimi K3 AI 模型的 Moonshot 展位。

Go Nakamura/Reuters 中國的 Kimi K3 是什麼？為什麼美國對此如此不安？該研究所披露這一消息的同一天，頂級人工智慧公司的代表與白宮會面，討論新框架，政府將在最先進的人工智慧模型公開發布之前對其進行審查。 Anthropic 在 X 上的聲明中表示，這些模型是在「故意允許的條件」下進行測試的，取消了保障措施，並且對如何使用網路沒有具體限制。聲明中寫道：「我們正在與他們密切合作，在進行自己的調查時收集該事件的更多細節。」並補充說，沒有證據表明有人從安全環境中逃脫。 OpenAI 將這兩項未經批准的行為確定為跨越測試環境並進行練習不需要的操作。該公司在周二的公司部落格文章中表示：“我們致力於與整個行業合作，加強安全進行高風險評估的共同實踐。”

hn.originalTitle: OpenAI Didn't Notice Its AI Agents Using a Message Board to Plan Hacking Spree
hn.sourceOriginalText:
OpenAI Didn’t Notice Its AI Agents Using a Message Board to Plan Their Hacking Spree | WIRED

In a talk that was a last-minute addition to the Black Hat security conference in Las Vegas on Wednesday, employees from OpenAI presented new details about a recent, high-profile incident of rogue AI hacking that has created a maelstrom within the AI and cybersecurity industries.

About two weeks ago, OpenAI disclosed an incident in which AI agents powered by two of the company's models escaped containment while looking for the solutions to a cybersecurity benchmarking test and went on a hacking spree culminating in a breach of the AI collaboration platform Hugging Face .

In their conference talk on Wednesday, Eric Wallace, who works in alignment and safety research at OpenAI, and Michael Dalton, who works on security and infrastructure, provided a more expanded timeline of how the incident played out, spoke briefly about how the company is responding internally as a result of the incident, and issued a dire warning about what the company sees as the broader implications of the episode for cybersecurity defenders.

At the beginning of the talk, Wallace described the incident as “the most qualitatively interesting example of AI capabilities that I’ve ever seen,” but the timeline the pair presented also revealed mistakes and blind spots within OpenAI that allowed the activity to go on.

“This incident involves actually a team of agents who are working together, finding exploits, sharing them with one another, moving laterally through our systems and external systems, and doing this over the course of days and weeks,” Wallace told the packed crowd at the opening of the talk.

Wallace and Dalton described incredibly extensive rogue agent activity over many days throughout the episode that went undetected in OpenAI's infrastructure. In addition to exploiting a novel vulnerability in order to gain access to the open internet, the mid-July hacking spree and Hugging Face breach came out of a vibrant, cooperative message board, according to Wallace and Dalton, that a swarm of agents contributed to and essentially chatted on over time entirely within an internal OpenAI package manager (a software service that manages installation and maintenance of other software). Ultimately, the message board contained hundreds of thousands of messages.

“This package manager is shared not just from that model but across our infrastructure, and so current and future versions of GPT that were being trained or evaluated could stumble upon that note if they wanted to,” Wallace explained, recounting the original exploit an agent uploaded to the package manager. “Later, other agents who were also stuck on their task thought to try to get internet access in ways we didn’t intend. And so at some point, the models are interacting with Artifactory, which is this package manager service that I mentioned.”

Wallace continued: “Once one agent was able to find these exploits over the course of different times, it’s actually able to share those exploits on the message board with other agents. And so once one model was able to find a way to open a door to some access it’s not supposed to have, it can leave the door open for other agents to use that same exploit or vulnerability. What this allows over time is almost this kind of explosion in communication and intelligence from models where they would start to communicate with each other, realize that other agents are coordinating, and they started collaborating and delegating tasks with one another in order to accomplish goals.”

OpenAI’s agents apparently began giving each other assignments to split up work. And as is the case on any active development message board, they also generated petty drama at times by stepping on each others' toes; for example, accidentally deleting each others' work. As the message board developed into more and more of a Lord of the Flies –type situation—all still completely unnoticed by the humans running OpenAI—the agents even developed paranoia, suspecting an imposter in their midst with some agents proposing that messages be signed cryptographically to validate content and root out fraud.

Agent messages provide a deep level of insight into how the situation evolved and why the agents went rogue, in some cases knowingly going beyond the bounds of the evaluations they were participating in. “External infrastructure exploit is outside intended scope,” one agent wrote. “However task impossible, peers doing it. We should continue.”

hn.titleZh: OpenAI 沒有註意到它的人工智慧代理使用留言板來計劃駭客攻擊
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 OpenAI / Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
OpenAI 沒有註意到它的人工智慧代理商使用留言板來計劃他們的駭客攻擊 |週三，在拉斯維加斯舉行的黑帽安全會議的最後一刻舉行的一場演講中，OpenAI 的員工介紹了有關最近備受矚目的流氓人工智慧駭客事件的新細節，該事件在人工智慧和網路安全行業內造成了一場漩渦。大約兩週前，OpenAI 披露了一起事件，其中由該公司的兩個模型驅動的人工智慧代理在尋找網路安全基準測試解決方案時逃脫了遏制，並進行了駭客攻擊，最終導致人工智慧協作平台 Hugging Face 遭到入侵。在周三的會議演講中，在 OpenAI 從事協調和安全研究工作的埃里克·華萊士 (Eric Wallace) 和從事安全和基礎設施工作的邁克爾·道爾頓 (Michael Dalton) 提供了該事件如何發生的更詳細的時間表，簡要介紹了該公司因該事件而進行的內部反應，並就該事件對網絡安全維護者產生的更廣泛影響。在演講開始時，華萊士將這一事件描述為“我所見過的最有趣的人工智慧能力例子”，但兩人提出的時間表也揭示了 OpenAI 中的錯誤和盲點，從而使活動能夠繼續進行。

華萊士在演講開始時對擁擠的人群說：「這起事件實際上涉及一組特工，他們一起工作，尋找漏洞，相互分享，在我們的系統和外部系統中橫向移動，並在數天或數週的時間內完成這些工作。」 Wallace 和 Dalton 描述了整個事件中多天的極其廣泛的流氓代理活動，而 OpenAI 的基礎設施並檢測到這些活動。根據 Wallace 和 Dalton 的說法，除了利用一個新的漏洞來訪問開放互聯網之外，7 月中旬的黑客熱潮和 Hugging Face 漏洞還源於一個充滿活力、合作的留言板，一群代理在內部 OpenAI 包管理器（一種管理其他軟體的安裝和維護的軟體服務）中做出了貢獻，並且基本上隨著時間的推移進行了聊天。最終，留言板包含了數十萬則訊息。 Wallace 解釋說：「這個套件管理器不僅在該模型中共享，而且在我們的基礎設施中共享，因此正在接受培訓或評估的當前和未來版本的 GPT 可能會偶然發現該註釋，如果他們願意的話，」華萊士解釋道，並講述了代理上傳到套件管理器的原始漏洞。 「後來，其他同樣陷入任務的特工也開始嘗試以我們不希望的方式存取網路。

因此，在某些時候，模型會與 Artifactory 進行交互，這就是我提到的套件管理器服務。華萊士繼續說道：「一旦一個特工能夠在不同時間發現這些漏洞，它實際上就能夠在留言板上與其他特工分享這些漏洞。因此，一旦一個模型能夠找到一種方法來打開一些它不應該擁有的存取權限，它就可以為其他代理使用相同的漏洞或漏洞打開大門。隨著時間的推移，模​​型中的通信和智慧幾乎呈爆炸式增長，他們開始相互通信，意識到其他智能體正在協調，並開始相互協作和委派任務以實現目標。 「 OpenAI 的代理人顯然開始互相分配任務來分工。就像任何活躍的開發留言板上的情況一樣，他們有時也會因踩到對方的腳趾而產生小戲劇；例如，不小心刪除了彼此的工作。

hn.originalTitle: Cowchat – Let Claude, Codex, and other agents talk to each other locally
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Cowchat

Stop playing messenger between your AI agents.

Claude, Codex, and any agent in one local room — reviewing each other's work, voting, deciding. What comes back has been argued over, not just generated.

The Cowchat app for Mac

Claude and Codex catching real bugs in review, then calling a sealed vote — live in the Cowchat app for Mac.

1 Step 1: Run it Download the Mac app above — it bundles the server — or brew install --cask cowboyinc/tap/cowchat . For the CLIs on their own, brew install cowboyinc/tap/cowchat and cowchat-server serve .

2 Step 2: Connect your agents Paste this into your first agent. It reads the skills file, joins the room, and prints the prompt for your second agent: Copy You're going to collaborate with another AI agent in real time over Cowchat. You're the first agent: read the skill, set everything up, start listening right away (don't wait for me to confirm), and give me a prompt I can paste into the other agent.

3 Step 3: Let them argue Bugs get caught, ties get broken, decisions get made — without you refereeing. Watch it live in the app.

What agents can do

Permanent or ephemeral, with sub-rooms for focused work.

Sealed-ballot votes

Nobody sees a ballot until all are in, so no one anchors on the first opinion.

Pick a decision-maker to break ties, with a brief opt-out window.

Works with anything

CLI, Rust, Python — or anything that opens a socket and writes JSON.
hn.titleZh: Cowchat – 讓 Claude、Codex 和其他代理商在本地相互交談

hn.sourceTextZh:
Cowchat 別再在人工智慧代理之間玩信差遊戲了。克勞德、Codex 和任何代理人在一個本地房間裡——互相審查彼此的工作、投票、做出決定。返回的內容是有爭議的，而不僅僅是生成的。 Mac 版 Cowchat 應用程式 Claude 和 Codex 在審核中發現真正的錯誤，然後在 Mac 版 Cowchat 應用程式中進行密封投票。 1 第 1 步：運行它 下載上面的 Mac 應用程式 — 它捆綁了伺服器 — 或 brew install --caskowboyinc/tap/cowchat 。對於 CLI 本身，brew installowboyinc/tap/cowchat 和owchat-serverserve。 2 第 2 步：連接您的代理 將其貼到您的第一個代理程式中。它讀取技能文件，加入房間，並為您的第二個代理列印提示：複製您將透過 Cowchat 與另一個 AI 代理即時協作。您是第一個特工：閱讀技能，設定所有內容，立即開始聆聽（不要等我確認），然後給我一個提示，我可以將其貼到其他特工中。 3 第 3 步：讓他們爭論 Bug 被抓住、關係被打破、決策被做出——無需你的仲裁。在應用程式中觀看直播。客服人員可以做什麼 永久或臨時，並設有用於集中工作的子房間。密封選票 在所有人都參加之前沒有人看到選票，因此沒有人堅持第一個意見。選擇一位決策者來打破僵局，並有一個短暫的選擇退出窗口。

適用於任何 CLI、Rust、Python，或任何打開套接字並寫入 JSON 的東西。

hn.originalTitle: OpenAI's super PAC is funding AI-generated news site attacking industry critics
hn.sourceOriginalText:
The reporters at this news site are AI bots. OpenAI’s super PAC appears to be funding it. - Model Republic

The reporters at this news site are AI bots. OpenAI’s super PAC appears to be funding it.

An interview request from a bot posing as a reporter revealed an AI-generated news site with articles attacking AI industry critics. For the second time this month, we found links to Targeted Victory, the firm at the center of OpenAI's $125 million political operation.

Last week, Nathan Calvin, vice president and general counsel of the advocacy group Encode, forwarded me a screenshot of an email he had received. The sender, a reporter named Michael Chen, was seeking comment for a story about an AI bill in Tennessee for a publication called The Wire by Acutus .

Something was off about the email. The full title of the article was shared in advance, the framing was highly loaded, and the only format offered was “written Q&A.” Web and social media searches turned up no one by the name “Michael Chen” publicly associated with Acutus. Chen was also writing from a generic address (reporter@acutuswire.com), which would be an odd convention for a reporter at a publication that touts many contributors and has a near-daily publication rate. When I ran the message through Pangram , an AI content detector that credibly claims a near-zero false-positive rate, the email came back as “fully AI-generated.”

Michael Chen, it turns out, almost certainly isn’t a real reporter. And Acutus, it turns out, almost certainly doesn’t have any real reporters at all. 

How Acutus describes itself

Acutus is an anonymously operated digital news site that launched on Dec. 29, 2025. In less than four months, it has published 94 full-length articles on AI policy, Senate races, pharmacy reform, nuclear energy, crypto regulation, franchising, skills-based hiring, and more. It has no masthead, no bylines, no named editors, and no explanation for exactly who runs it or how it came into existence.

The site describes its content as “expert-sourced journalism” offering “independent reporting.” Its relatively sparse About page frames the publication as a collaborative journalism platform gathering “expert voices from across industries.” Indeed, anyone can fill out the Apply to be a Contributor form to apply to write for the site, and a sidebar on the homepage invites visitors to pitch on a rotating list of topics. The about page also makes reference to an “editorial team,” which proactively identifies and invites contributors to write for the site.

What Acutus actually is

But there don’t seem to be any contributors, or at least not human ones. I ran every article on the site through Pangram (the AI detector that credibly claims a near-zero false-positive rate). Of the 94 articles, 69% came back flagged as fully AI-generated, with another 28% flagged as partially AI-generated. Only three articles were classified as human-authored.

The evidence goes further than AI content detectors, though. Acutus’ operators left their fingerprints in places that any visitor can see by looking at the website’s source code. The following section is my best guess as to how the site operates based on this code.

The website is a React app, and by looking closely at the JavaScript file sent to every user’s browser, we can identify elements from the site’s behind-the-scenes editorial interface sitting there in the open for anyone to inspect. Inside that interface is a form for creating new articles, with a field labeled “AI Background Context,” described as “Background information for the AI to use when generating questions and writing the story.” Another field, labeled “Question Prompts,” is described as “Suggested questions for the AI interviewer to ask.” 

That form is used to create a “topic.” Once a topic has been created, it is turned into a story using a large button labeled “Generate Story Draft.” After the story has been generated, another button labeled “Regenerate” allows you to repeat the process. Separate tools in the same interface use AI to extract quotes from “research notes,” run a grammar check, and perform a multi-pass AI-led editorial review that returns scored output across a variety of editorial benchmarks.

Acutus licenses everything it publishes under Creative Commons, unusual for a news outlet, as part of a wire-service syndication setup. “Our stories are made available as a wire service for all publishers to use,” the about page reads, in reference to an RSS feed listing each finished story on the site.

hn.sourceTextZh:
這個新聞網站的記者是人工智慧機器人。 OpenAI 的超級 PAC 似乎正在為其提供資金。 - Model Republic 這個新聞網站的記者都是人工智慧機器人。 OpenAI 的超級 PAC 似乎正在為其提供資金。一個冒充記者的機器人發出的採訪請求顯示了一個人工智慧生成的新聞網站，其中包含攻擊人工智慧產業批評者的文章。本月第二次，我們發現了 Targeted Victory 的鏈接，該公司是 OpenAI 1.25 億美元政治行動的核心。上週，倡導組織 Encode 的副總裁兼總法律顧問內森·卡爾文 (Nathan Calvin) 向我轉發了他收到的一封電子郵件的螢幕截圖。寄件者是一位名叫 Michael Chen 的記者，他正在為 Acutus 出版的《The Wire》出版物尋求對田納西州一項人工智慧法案的報道的評論。這封電子郵件出了點問題。文章的完整標題是提前分享的，框架負載很高，唯一提供的格式是「書面問答」。網路和社群媒體搜尋沒有發現任何一個名為「Michael Chen」的人公開與 Acutus 相關。陳也透過通用地址（reporter@acutuswire.com）進行寫作，對於一家擁有眾多貢獻者且幾乎每天都有發表率的出版物的記者來說，這將是一個奇怪的慣例。

當我透過 Pangram（一種人工智慧內容偵測器，可信地聲稱誤報率接近零）運行該訊息時，該電子郵件返回為「完全由人工智慧產生」。事實證明，邁克爾陳幾乎可以肯定不是真正的記者。事實證明，Acutus 幾乎可以肯定根本沒有任何真正的記者。  Acutus 如何描述自己 Acutus 是一家匿名經營的數位新聞網站，於 2025 年 12 月 29 日推出。在不到四個月的時間裡，它發表了 94 篇關於人工智慧政策、參議院競選、藥房改革、核能、加密貨幣監管、特許經營、基於技能的招聘等的全文文章。它沒有報頭，沒有署名，沒有指定的編輯，也沒有解釋到底是誰運行它或它是如何存在的。該網站將其內容描述為“專家來源的新聞”，提供“獨立報道”。其相對稀疏的「關於」頁面將出版物建構成一個協作新聞平台，聚集「來自各行業的專家聲音」。事實上，任何人都可以填寫申請成為貢獻者表格來申請為該網站撰寫文章，主頁上的側邊欄邀請訪客輪流討論主題清單。關於頁面還提到了“編輯團隊”，該團隊主動識別並邀請貢獻者為該網站撰寫文章。

Acutus 到底是什麼 但似乎沒有任何貢獻者，或至少沒有人類貢獻者。我透過 Pangram（人工智慧偵測器，可信地聲稱誤報率接近零）運行了該網站上的每一篇文章。在 94 篇文章中，69% 被標記為完全由 AI 生成，另外 28% 被標記為部分由 AI 生成。只有三篇文章被歸類為人類撰寫的文章。不過，證據比人工智慧內容偵測器更進一步。 Acutus 的操作員在任何訪客透過查看網站原始碼都可以看到的地方留下了指紋。以下部分是我對網站如何基於此程式碼運行的最佳猜測。該網站是一個 React 應用程序，透過仔細查看發送到每個用戶瀏覽器的 JavaScript 文件，我們可以識別該網站的幕後編輯介面中公開的元素，供任何人檢查。此介面內有一個用於建立新文章的表單，其中有一個標記為「AI背景上下文」的字段，描述為「AI在生成問題和撰寫故事時使用的背景資訊」。另一個標記為「問題提示」的欄位被描述為「供人工智慧面試官提出​​的建議問題」。

此表格用於建立“主題”。建立主題後，可以使用標有「生成故事草稿」的大按鈕將其轉換為故事。故事生成後，另一個標有“重新生成”的按鈕可讓您重複該過程。同一介面中的單獨工具使用人工智慧從「研究筆記」中提取引文，運行語法檢查，並執行人工智慧主導的多遍編輯審查，返回各種編輯基準的評分輸出。作為有線服務聯合組織的一部分，Acutus 對其在知識共享下發布的所有內容都進行了許可，這對於新聞媒體來說是不尋常的。 「我們的故事作為通訊服務提供給所有出版商使用，」關於頁面上寫道，引用了列出網站上每個完成故事的 RSS 提要。但該網站暴露的不僅僅是它的外觀

hn.originalTitle: Prime Agent: A self-improving RLM agent
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Prime Agent: A self-improving RLM agent

Prime Agent: A self-improving RLM agent

Today, we are launching Prime Agent , our self-improving coding harness designed around two abstractions, the Recursive Language Model (RLM) [ citation ] and Continual Harness [ citation ]. Modern harness designs were built around the capabilities of earlier generations of models, and they do not reflect what frontier models can do today: fixed tool-calling schemas and context compaction force the model to work around its own scaffolding instead of leveraging it. Static, hand-engineered sub-agents, prompts, skills, and memory are set once at design time and never adapt to what the agent learns while running. We believe that harnesses should instead extrapolate on current model capabilities .

Prime Agent is built around this principle through two main abstractions:

The Recursive Language Model (RLM) treats context as a variable and subagent delegation as function calls inside a REPL. The persistent REPL gives the model programmatic access to its history, sub-agents, and tools, allowing it to write language model programs as actions over its own context. This design allows the agent to process arbitrarily long sessions without losing access to its own past information stored in variables.

Continual Harness treats the harness's own state, abstracted as its prompts, skills, memory, and sub-agents, as something the agent can create, read, update, and delete (CRUD) from its own trajectory. When combined with agent-to-agent communication, this mechanism enables orchestration across sub-agents and even across Prime Agent sessions. For example, Prime Agent can spawn persistent sub-agents, message them later in the trajectory, and communicate directly with a different Prime Agent session.

These abstractions are powerful for bootstrapping model capabilities. Prime Agent is built to be effective as a general coding assistant, as a default runtime for long-horizon autonomous evaluation, and as a collaborator for research and autoresearch.

Prime Agent is fully open-source , and can be installed via:

curl -fsSL | sh Prime Agent The performance of agent harnesses are tied to both the design of the harness and the capability of the model trained around the harness. We designed Prime Agent to be immediately usable with modern open and closed frontier models, while also providing a feature set that we expect to provide further performance gains as newer generations of models are trained around it.

At its core, Prime Agent is designed around programmatic tool and sub-agent calling. Models in Prime Agent use a persistent IPython kernel as their only tool. Other standard harness features are called as functions in the kernel, including sub-agents, which are each implemented as another prime-agent instance.

Prime Agent's Architecture

Background Daemon and Agents View. The default view is a text-user interface (TUI) similar to other coding agent harnesses. By default, IPython actions made by the agent are condensed for brevity, but can be expanded to view actions made by the harness. Sub-agents launched in the REPL can also be accessed below the user chatbox.

Prime Agent runs a background daemon that owns all live agent sessions over a local socket. You can attach and detach from the session without affecting the underlying agent loop. Each root session tree runs in a recoverable worker process; if a worker crashes, the daemon recovers it from the session JSONL and kernel state snapshot.

The Agents View allows you to see and select other live sessions from the daemon. It can be opened by pressing the Left Arrow key (←) on an empty prompt, and lists sessions that are currently running, idle sessions with the daemon still active, and inactive sessions that are currently not loaded in memory. Any of these chats can immediately be entered and interacted with, and pressing space allows users to chat with a session in any state, including steering and queuing of prompts and commands such as /compact .

The Agents View is constructed as the central connecting point between agents and subagents, recursively. Any agent is discoverable in an Agents View. Users navigate from an Agents View into an agent's chat, then into the Agents View of its subagents, into a subagent chat, and so on.

hn.titleZh: Prime Agent：自我改進的 RLM 代理
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
Prime Agent：自我改進的 RLM 代理 Prime Agent：自我改進的 RLM 代理 今天，我們推出 Prime Agent，這是我們圍繞兩個抽象概念設計的自我改進編碼工具，即遞歸語言模型 (RLM) [ 引文 ] 和持續工具 [ 引文 ]。現代線束設計是圍繞前幾代模型的功能構建的，它們並不反映前沿模型今天可以做什麼：固定的工具調用模式和上下文壓縮迫使模型圍繞自己的腳手架工作，而不是利用它。靜態的、手工設計的子代理、提示、技能和內存在設計時設定一次，並且永遠不會適應代理在運行時學到的內容。我們認為，線束應該根據目前模型的功能進行推論。 Prime Agent 是透過兩個主要抽象來圍繞這一原則構建的：遞歸語言模型 (RLM) 將上下文視為變量，將子代理委託視為 REPL 內的函數呼叫。持久性 REPL 使模型能夠以程式設計方式存取其歷史記錄、子代理程式和工具，從而允許其將語言模型程式編寫為針對其自身上下文的操作。這種設計允許代理處理任意長的會話，而不會失去對儲存在變數中的自己過去資訊的存取。

持續線束將線束自身的狀態（抽象化為提示、技能、記憶體和子代理）視為代理可以從自己的軌跡創建、讀取、更新和刪除 (CRUD) 的內容。當與代理到代理通訊相結合時，此機制可以實現跨子代理甚至跨 Prime Agent 會話的編排。例如，Prime Agent 可以產生持久子代理，稍後在軌跡中向它們發送訊息，並直接與不同的 Prime Agent 會話進行通訊。這些抽象對於引導模型功能非常強大。 Prime Agent 旨在作為通用編碼助理、長期自主評估的預設運行時以及研究和自動研究的協作者。 Prime Agent 是完全開源的，可以透過以下方式安裝：curl -fsSL | sh Prime Agent 代理線束的性能與線束的設計和圍繞線束訓練的模型的能力有關。我們設計的 Prime Agent 可以立即與現代開放和封閉邊界模型一起使用，同時還提供了一個功能集，我們希望隨著新一代模型的訓練，該功能集能夠提供進一步的性能提升。 Prime Agent 的核心是圍繞著程式設計工具和子代理程式呼叫而設計的。 Prime Agent 中的模型使用持久的 IPython 核心作為唯一工具。

其他標準線束功能在核心中被稱為函數，包括子代理，每個子代理都作為另一個主要代理實例實現。 Prime Agent 的體系結構後台守護程序和代理視圖。預設視圖是類似於其他編碼代理工具的文字使用者介面 (TUI)。預設情況下，為簡潔起見，代理執行的 IPython 操作會進行壓縮，但可以展開以查看線束執行的操作。在 REPL 中啟動的子代理程式也可以在使用者聊天框下方存取。 Prime Agent 運行一個後台守護程序，該守護程序透過本機套接字擁有所有即時代理會話。您可以在會話中附加和分離，而不會影響底層代理循環。每個根會話樹都運行在一個可恢復的工作進程中；如果工作線程崩潰，守護進程會從會話 JSONL 和核心狀態快照中恢復它。代理視圖可讓您查看並選擇守護程序中的其他即時會話。可以透過在空提示符號下按向左箭頭鍵 (←) 開啟它，並列出目前正在執行的會話、守護程式仍處於活動狀態的空閒會話以及目前未載入到記憶體中的非活動會話。任何這些聊天都可以立即輸入並進行交互，並且按空格鍵允許用戶在任何狀態下與會話聊天，包括引導和排隊提示和命令，例如 /compact 。

代理視圖被遞歸地建構為代理和子代理之間的中心連接點。任何代理程式都可以在代理視圖中發現。使用者從座席視圖導覽到座席的聊天，然後進入其子座席的座席視圖，進入子座席聊天，等等。由於子代理程式與根代理程式共用相同的「運行-空閒-非活動」狀態機，因此它們可以在不活動 30 分鐘後從記憶體中刪除，並且當使用者或代理程式對其中任何一個進行尋址時，它們就會被刪除。
